articles.title: Housing downturn accelerates, oil prices fall
articles.description: Australia's property downturn is accelerating - and widening - as higher interest rates and unease over tax changes continue to impact buyer activity. The latest data from Cotality shows national property prices fell 0.7 per cent in July. For more, Jasmine Kassis spoke with Cotality Head of Research Gerard Burg. Also, the Australian share market reversed earlier losses to finish higher, helped by oil prices falling more than five per cent as Donald Trump called off planned strikes on Iran. For more, Rena Sarumpaet spoke with Sarto Advisory analyst David Walsh.

articles.title: US stocks rally near a record as falling oil prices ease Wall Street's worries about inflation
articles.description: U.S. stocks rallied to the edge of their all-time high after easing oil prices helped calm Wall Street’s worries that inflation could get even worse. The S&P 500 jumped 1.5% Monday and is just 0.1% below its record set earlier this summer. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.3%, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 2.1%. Brent crude's price fell 4.7% after President Donald Trump said he would hold off on ordering new strikes against Iran. That helped Treasury yields to fall in the bond market. Stocks of airlines and other companies with big fuel bills rallied.

articles.title: US stocks: Dow closes at record high on Iran talks optimism
articles.description: US stocks opened August with strong gains, pushing the Dow Industrials to a record closing high. Easing oil prices and Treasury yields supported the market's upward movement. Communication services sector led gains, while energy experienced a decline. Amazon's market value surpassed three trillion dollars for the first time. Investors are now focused on upcoming economic data and corporate earnings reports.
